leads.name: Zeebrugge Raid memorial lime, Admiraal Keyesplein
leads.reason: The register object combines a 1998-unveiled WWI memorial (fragments of the Zeebrugge Mole the ship Vindictive struck in the 1918 raid) with a lime planted alongside it only in 2016 (a silver lime, Tilia tomentosa, per the register's supplementary text -- note this conflicts with the object's own kenmerkgroep species field, which lists Tilia europaea). At ~10 years old the tree itself is not old, spectacular or independently historic; the monument is the real heritage subject, the tree is incidental. Also 13.7km from Bruges centre in Zeebrugge, a distinct coastal deelgemeente (a real train connection exists, roughly 15-20 minutes, but this was not the reason for rejection). Could be revisited if the project ever wants a dedicated Zeebrugge entry, or if the tree matures and gains its own story.

leads.name: Peace lime, Gaston Roelandtsplein
leads.reason: The original 1920 peace lime (planted for the WWI armistice) was removed in 2015 for disease and instability, and replaced in 2016 with a new young lime on an underground root-support structure. Current tree is ~10 years old: historically resonant site (a war memorial by Gustaaf Pickery stands centrally, the square is named for executed resistance fighter Gaston Roelandts) but the living tree itself does not clear the old/spectacular bar yet.

blocked.name: Gekandelaarde zilverlinde 'De Keizer', Polderstraat
blocked.reason: Private land. Register's own text: 'In de met een hekken afgesloten voortuin bij de Villa Hortensia' -- in the fenced-off front garden of a private villa. Blocked under hard rule 10 regardless of the tree's real horticultural interest (a candelabra-grafted silver lime).

blocked.name: Wych elm, Sint-Salvatorskerkhof
blocked.reason: Confirmed dead. The register's own 2019-11-27 supplementary note states plainly: 'Onroerend Erfgoed heeft vastgesteld dat de iep inmiddels gerooid is' (Onroerend Erfgoed has established that the elm has since been felled). A rare surviving wych elm (389cm girth in 2013, most Belgian elms killed by Dutch elm disease) but gone. Never ships.

blocked.name: Pollarded limes, Sint-Gilliskerk
blocked.reason: Not a single collectible point: a row of four (originally six) pollarded limes along Lange Raamstraat plus one more at a nearby corner, described only vaguely ('gezien hun omvang zijn deze vermoedelijk al van een behoorlijke leeftijd' -- probably fairly old, going by their size). Same shape as an avenue: nothing to stand at, no measurements, no single named tree.

blocked.name: Pollarded limes, Sint-Pietersbandenkerk churchyard, Dudzele
blocked.reason: Not a single collectible point: the register describes a row of pollarded limes tracing the perimeter and paths of the churchyard, no individual tree named, no age or girth recorded. Was the brief's suggested reserve candidate but does not clear the collectible-point bar. Also 7.3km from Bruges centre in Dudzele, a separate village deelgemeente, which would need its own transport check if ever revisited.

blocked.name: Double oak avenue, Bisschopsdreef
blocked.reason: An avenue (dubbele opgaande eikendreef), not a collectible point. Per the brief's own instruction to avoid the avenues.

blocked.name: Lime and maple avenue planting, Leopold I-laan
blocked.reason: An avenue planting (laanbeplanting), not a collectible point. Per the brief's own instruction to avoid the avenues.
